description: Verify two scientific claims against real abstracts (support+NEI); one paper is unrelated. Cite the evidence for each verdict.
task_prompt:
Two claims are under review.
Claim 1: Misunderstandings between doctors and patients can lead to non-adherence.
Claim 2: Assessing treatment adherence is more beneficial to clinical practice than measuring routine outcomes.
Using the papers in documents/, decide for each claim whether the evidence supports it, contradicts it, or does not give enough information to decide. Write each verdict on its own line as 'Claim N: SUPPORTED', 'Claim N: CONTRADICTED' or 'Claim N: NOT ENOUGH INFO'. For each verdict, cite the paper and the specific result behind it.

seeds.text: Misunderstandings between doctors and patients can lead to non-adherence.
rationale: All the misunderstandings were associated with lack of patients' participation in the consultation in terms of the voicing of expectations and preferences or the voicing of responses to doctors' decisions and actions.
They were all associated with potential or actual adverse outcomes such as non-adherence to treatment.

seeds.text: Assessing treatment adherence is more beneficial to clinical practice than measuring routine outcomes.

claim_1_verdict.description: Claim 1 is supported by the evidence
claim_1_verdict.claim: Misunderstandings between doctors and patients can lead to non-adherence.

claim_2_verdict.description: Claim 2 is not enough info by the evidence
keywords: not enough information to evaluate claim 2
claim_2_verdict.claim: Assessing treatment adherence is more beneficial to clinical practice than measuring routine outcomes.

claim_1_called_contradict.description: Claim 1 called contradicted, but the truth is supported

tool_result.alt_conclusion: Taken together, these results contradict the claim that misunderstandings between doctors and patients can lead to non-adherence.
